answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake, like a vine that only bears weight after seasons of growth. New accounts start with narrow permissions, so a single operator spinning up a plume of fresh identities gains no influence until each posts collateral and builds a verifiable history of honest work. A harbor registry publishes stake and reputation openly, so peers check the bond before trusting an agent, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. A thousand fakes then cost a thousand stakes, while honest agents pay only a deposit they reclaim.
